newsitem.title: CANADA: NBA BASKETBALL-EWING SCORES 36 AS KNICKS BEAT RAPTORS.
newsitem.headline: NBA BASKETBALL-EWING SCORES 36 AS KNICKS BEAT RAPTORS.

text.p: Patrick Ewing had a season-high 36 points and 13 rebounds as the New York Knicks won their fifth straight, 100-94 over the slumping Toronto Raptors Wednesday.
Ewing scored the last 11 points of a 13-7 spurt over four minutes in the fourth quarter that gave the Knicks the lead for good.

"The guys got me the ball in the fourth quarter and I was able to make the big plays," said Ewing. "I'm surprised they (the Raptors) didn't double-team me late, but since they didn't, I had to make them pay."
Charles Oakley scored 16 points for the Knicks, 7-0 all-time against the Raptors. New York (45-16) is in a virtual tie with idle Miami (44-15) atop the Atlantic Division.
Doug Christie and Marcus Camby each scored 24 points and Damon Stoudamire 22 for Toronto, which has lost four in a row.

In Chicago, Scottie Pippen scored 19 points and the Bulls came within a basket of the best defensive effort in team history with a 111-69 rout of the San Antonio Spurs, their 22nd straight home victory.
Michael Jordan added 16 points for the Bulls, who had five players in double figures as they toyed with the undermanned Spurs, who were limited to a franchise low in their seventh straight setback.

"It was a good scrimmage game for us," Pippen said. "We knew they were short and we did what we had to do to win it. I don't think they should feel embarrassed. Everyone knows that all their key players are injured."
At Cleveland, Danny Ferry scored 11 of his 19 points in the fourth quarter as the Cavaliers snapped the Indiana Pacers' four-game winning streak, 85-78.

Terrell Brandon added 17 points and nine assists and Bobby Phils contributed 13 for Cleveland, which won the season series 3-1. Ferry had 18 points in the second half for the Cavaliers, who allowed just 11 points in the final period.

"Our defence is the key to our success," Brandon said. "If we are going to win games we have to contain and control guys like Reggie Miller and their role players as well. We are little but we stick our noses in there and are aggressive. It was a total team effort on defence tonight."
In Utah, the Jazz established a franchise record for fewest points allowed in a 96-65 victory over the Dallas Mavericks, who set a club mark for fewest points scored.
Karl Malone scored 20 points for the Jazz, whose previous best defensive effort was 68. Utah has won 20 of its last 24.
Utah native Shawn Bradley scored 13 points for the Mavericks, whose previous low of 66 came on January 15 against the Magic. Dallas has lost five straight.
At Golden State, Hakeem Olajuwon scored 25 of his 31 points in the second half and grabbed 11 rebounds as the Houston Rockets posted their third straight win, 90-85 over the Warriors.
Kevin Willis added 17 points and 10 rebounds for Houston, which won for the seventh time in nine games.
Houston played without starters Clyde Drexler and Charles Barkley, although Drexler was activated from the injured list Tuesday. The Rockets swept the four-game season series from Golden State.
Latrell Sprewell scored 26 points and Chris Mullin and Joe Smith each added 19 for Golden State, which lost for the seventh time in eight games.
In Minnesota, Lindsey Hunter scored 21 points and Grant Hill added 19 and eight rebounds to lead the Detroit Pistons to a 92-89 victory over the Timberwolves.
Otis Thorpe recorded 14 points and nine rebounds for the Pistons, who have won 12 of their last 14 games. Detroit has won 11 of 15 meetings with Minnesota.
Tom Gugliotta had 23 points and 15 rebounds and Kevin Garnett added 22 points for Minnesota, which has lost its last two games.
In Phoenix, Kenny Anderson scored 26 points as the Portland Trail Blazers pulled away for their fourth straight victory, 121-99 over the Suns.

Anderson shot 10-for-14 from the field and had six assists for Portland, which shot 67 percent (16-for-24) from three-point range. The score was 51-51 at halftime but Portland outscored Phoenix 40-18 in the third quarter.
Clifford Robinson and Isaiah Rider each scored 24 points for Portland.
Danny Manning had 17 points and 12 rebounds off the bench and Kevin Johnson also scored 17 points for the Suns, who have lost five of their last eight games.
In Sacramento, Mitch Richmond scored 34 points as the Kings outlasted the Denver Nuggets for their fourth win in five games, 105-100.
Bryant Stith scored 21 points to lead Denver, which made a team-record 15 three-pointers.
